title: CATARACT 2, MULTIPLE TYPES
alt_titles: CATARACT 2, MULTIPLE TYPES, WITH OR WITHOUT MICROCORNEA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cataract-2 (CTRCT2), which comprises several types of cataract, with or without microcornea, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gamma-C-crystallin gene (CRYGC; 123680) on chromosome 2q33.

checks.claim: Cataract-2 (CTRCT2) comprises several types of cataract, with or without microcornea.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation has been associated with the phenotype of lamellar cataract but is also considered a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the NCBI database.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports more than one cataract type (nuclear in this family, lamellar in an earlier report) but says nothing about microcornea.

checks.claim: Cataract-2 (CTRCT2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gamma-C-crystallin gene (CRYGC).
checks.evidence_quote: a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member and is absent from both unaffected family members and unaffected controls
checks.explanation: Every affected family member carries the mutation in one allele (heterozygous) of CRYGC, which supports the causal link.

checks.claim: The CRYGC gene is located on chromosome 2q33.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention CRYGC specifically or any chromosomal location; this may be in the full text or other sources but is absent from the supplied abstract.

paragraphs.text: Mutations in the CRYGC gene have been found in several forms of congenital or early-onset cataract. These include Coppock-like (nuclear) cataract, zonular pulverulent cataract, and lamellar cataract. Some affected people also have microcornea. Inheritance is autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Mutations in the CRYGC gene have been found in several forms of congenital or early-onset cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Our finding expands the spectrum of CRYGC mutations associated with congenital cataract and confirms the role of gamma-crystallin in the pathogenesis of congenital nuclear cataracts.
checks.explanation: The paper describes multiple CRYGC mutations associated with congenital cataracts.

checks.claim: Coppock-like (nuclear) cataract is one of the cataract forms caused by CRYGC mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: A CRYGC mutation was found in the Coppock-like cataract family.

checks.claim: Zonular pulverulent cataract is one of the cataract forms caused by CRYGC mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.explanation: Zonular pulverulent cataract is associated with a CRYGC mutation.

checks.claim: Lamellar cataract is one of the cataract forms caused by CRYGC mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation has been associated with the phenotype of lamellar cataract
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the CRYGC R168W mutation has been associated with lamellar cataract.

checks.claim: Some individuals with CRYGC-related cataract also have microcornea.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel nonsense mutation in CRYGC in a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataracts and microcornea.
checks.explanation: Affected members of this CRYGC family have microcornea.

checks.claim: CRYGC-related cataract is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.evidence_quote: A seven-generation family with 30 members affected by highly variable autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataracts has been previously described.
checks.explanation: The paper states that inheritance is autosomal dominant.

paragraphs.text: In the families reported with CRYGC mutations, the cataract phenotype segregated as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.claim: In the families reported with CRYGC mutations, the cataract phenotype segregated as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: in a three-generation Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract
checks.explanation: The single family reported here shows autosomal dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Coppock-like cataract was mapped to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster on chromosome 2q33-q35. That cluster contains CRYGA through CRYGD.

checks.claim: Coppock-like cataract was mapped to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster on chromosome 2q33-q35.
checks.evidence_quote: The absolute correlation between the presence of haplotype P and cataract within this family shows that the gamma-crystallin gene cluster and the locus for the Coppock-like cataract are closely linked [logarithm of odds (lod) score of 7.58 at its maximum at phi = 0].
checks.explanation: Linkage of Coppock-like cataract to the gamma-crystallin cluster is stated, but the abstract gives no chromosomal location (2q33-q35).

checks.claim: The gamma-crystallin gene cluster on chromosome 2q33-q35 contains the genes CRYGA through CRYGD.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not list the genes in the cluster (CRYGA-CRYGD) or its chromosomal location.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant congenital cataract is genetically heterogeneous. Mutations in the neighboring CRYGD gene, which lies in the same gamma-crystallin cluster on chromosome 2q33, cause a separate form of cataract.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant congenital cataract is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital cataract is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous lens disorder
checks.explanation: The paper states that congenital cataract is genetically heterogeneous, with 34 loci, and that most families show autosomal dominant transmission.

checks.claim: The CRYGD gene lies near CRYGC in the same gamma-crystallin cluster on chromosome 2q33.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently mapped the aculeiform cataract to the gamma-crystallin locus (CRYG) on chromosome 2q33-35, and mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster identified the aculeiform-cataract mutation in exon 2 of gamma-crystallin D (CRYGD).
checks.explanation: CRYGD is in the same CRYG gene cluster on 2q33-35 that also contains CRYGC.

checks.claim: Mutations in the CRYGD gene cause a form of cataract separate from CRYGC-related cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster identified the aculeiform-cataract mutation in exon 2 of gamma-crystallin D (CRYGD).
checks.explanation: A CRYGD mutation causes aculeiform cataract, which is a different form from the CRYGC-related Coppock-like cataract.

paragraphs.text: Heon et al. (1999) studied families with autosomal dominant congenital cataract linked to the gamma-crystallin cluster. In a family with Coppock-like cataract, they found a heterozygous thr5-to-pro (T5P) mutation in the CRYGC gene. The mutation was predicted to disturb the folding of the protein.

checks.claim: Heon et al. (1999) studied families with autosomal dominant congenital cataract linked to the gamma-crystallin cluster.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently mapped the aculeiform cataract to the gamma-crystallin locus (CRYG) on chromosome 2q33-35
checks.explanation: The families were linked to the CRYG cluster, but the abstract does not say the inheritance was autosomal dominant or the cataract congenital.

checks.claim: Heon et al. (1999) found a heterozygous thr5-to-pro (T5P) mutation in the CRYGC gene in a family with Coppock-like cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: A CRYGC missense mutation is reported, but the abstract does not give T5P or zygosity. Those details would be in the full text.

checks.claim: The CRYGC T5P mutation was predicted to disturb the folding of the gamma-C-crystallin protein.
checks.explanation: The abstract links impaired folding to the CRYGD aculeiform mutation ('could be associated with an impaired folding of CRYGD'), not to the CRYGC mutation.

paragraphs.text: Ren et al. (2000) studied a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract. They identified a heterozygous 5-bp duplication (insertion) in the CRYGC gene that caused a frameshift and a truncated protein.

checks.claim: Ren et al. (2000) studied a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: A seven-generation family with 30 members affected by highly variable autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataracts has been previously described.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Ren et al. (2000) identified a heterozygous 5-bp duplication (insertion) in the CRYGC gene in a family with variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: 'One allele' means heterozygous. The title calls it a 5-base insertion.

checks.claim: The 5-bp duplication in CRYGC identified by Ren et al. (2000) caused a frameshift and a truncated protein.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence and is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids.
checks.explanation: The reading frame is disrupted (frameshift), and the predicted protein is truncated.

paragraphs.text: Santhiya et al. (2002) screened the gamma-crystallin genes in Indian families with autosomal dominant congenital cataract. In a family with lamellar cataract, they found a heterozygous arg168-to-trp (R168W) mutation in CRYGC.

checks.claim: Santhiya et al. (2002) screened the gamma-crystallin genes in Indian families with autosomal dominant congenital cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes cause autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.
checks.explanation: The title implies a study of gamma-crystallin genes in autosomal dominant congenital cataract. It does not mention screening or Indian families. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Santhiya et al. (2002) found a heterozygous arg168-to-trp (R168W) mutation in CRYGC in an Indian family with lamellar cataract.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied. It does not mention R168W, CRYGC, zygosity, an Indian family or lamellar cataract.

paragraphs.text: Heon et al. (1999) found a heterozygous thr5-to-pro (T5P) mutation in the CRYGC gene in a family with autosomal dominant Coppock-like cataract.

checks.claim: Heon et al. (1999) found a heterozygous thr5-to-pro (T5P) mutation in the CRYGC gene in a family with autosomal dominant Coppock-like cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: A CRYGC missense mutation in the Coppock-like family is reported, but the abstract does not give T5P, heterozygosity or autosomal dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Ren et al. (2000) found a heterozygous 5-bp duplication in the CRYGC gene in a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract. The duplication caused a frameshift that led to a truncated protein.

checks.claim: Ren et al. (2000) found a heterozygous 5-bp duplication in the CRYGC gene in a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: Heterozygous 5-bp duplication found in the family with autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataract.

checks.claim: The 5-bp duplication in CRYGC found by Ren et al. (2000) caused a frameshift leading to a truncated protein.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence and is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids.
checks.explanation: The frameshift leads to a truncated protein.

paragraphs.text: Santhiya et al. (2002) found a heterozygous arg168-to-trp (R168W) mutation in the CRYGC gene in an Indian family with autosomal dominant lamellar cataract.

checks.claim: Santhiya et al. (2002) found a heterozygous arg168-to-trp (R168W) mutation in the CRYGC gene in an Indian family with autosomal dominant lamellar cataract.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied. The specific variant, gene, zygosity, family and phenotype are not stated.
